replies.author: seanwilliams4620
replies.text: Hi Nate.  I had a Pur R/O water maker on my boat that I sailed to the Carribean and back every year for over a decade. Whenever the unit wasn't going to be used for a while I had to treat it with a biocide that would remain in the membrane for the duration of it not being used.  That fluid that came with your machine ought to have been a biocide.  I used to get 1 gallon of purified water and 50 gallons of "waste" brine and the  unit drew quite a few amps. Regardless it was such a treat having a virtually unlimited fresh water supply on deep sea passages. In essence a blue water sailboat like I had is one of the best preparedness platforms possible.  I believe the threats of storms and such are far outweighed by the benefits of mobility.  Thank you for all your efforts.

replies.author: Christian_Prepper
replies.text:
REALITY CHECK CASHED:
A person can generally use distilled water indefinitely for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and showering without developing any negative health problems simply because the water is distilled. Since distilled water contains virtually no minerals, fresh meats, fish, eggs, vegetables, nuts, and seeds can supply the necessary minerals and electrolytes. When cooking, retain broths and cooking liquids when practical to avoid discarding minerals that leach from food. The primary concerns are inadequate dietary nutrition, excessive water consumption that dilutes blood sodium, and electrolyte losses from heavy sweating, especially in hot climates. There is no scientifically established time limit after which distilled water becomes harmful; maintaining adequate nutrition, hydration, and electrolyte balance is far more important than how long the water has been distilled. Even if a person had no food, zero, and only distilled water to consume, they run the risk of dying of starvation long before experiencing any ill effects from distilled water.

newest.author: JohnHi6
newest.text: Drinking demineralised water doesn't pose a Legionnaires disease risk..... It can strip your body of the already present minerals and cause an electrolyte imbalance. But legionnaires disease isn't caught by drinking contaminated water (this filter would remove anyhow) it's primary transmission is by inhaling atomised droplets from a shower, humidifier or AC unit. One thing that puzzled me with this unit is that with RO filters there's normally 3 pipes. One is raw water in. One is fresh water out and the third is waste water from the high concentration side of the osmosis filter which with salinated water would carry the sodium chloride saturated water away from the filter. Without the third waste pipe RO filters get clogged very easily and although not drinkable this water is an important part of the fitters output.
